questions.solution:
Given:

$f ( x ) = e^{x}sinx$

We know that the slope of tangent is given by~\left\{\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f^{'}\left(x\right)\right\}$.

Now,

$f^{'} ( x ) = Z = e^{x}sinx + e^{x}cosx$

$Z = e^{x} \left(sinx + cosx\right)$

\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$e^{x} \left(sinx + cosx\right) + e^{x} \left(cosx - sinx\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$2e^{x}cosx$

For maxima,~\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$0$

$⇒ 2e^{x}cosx = 0$

$⇒ e^{x}cosx = 0$

$∵ e^{x} \ne 0, x \in R$~

$∴ cosx = 0 ⇒ x = $\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$; \left\{∵ x \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]\right\}$

Now,~

$⇒ $\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}} =$2e^{x}cosx - 2e^{x}sinx$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } $= 2e^{x} \left($cosx - sinx\right)$

\left$\${\$left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)$x = $\dfrac{π}{2}\right$\} = $-2e\dfrac{π}{2}< 0 \to \text{MAXIMA}$

And,~\left\{\left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right\} = 2e\dfrac{3\pi}{2} > 0 \to \text{MINIMA}$

Hence,~$Z = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \left(\text{slope of tangent}\right)~is maximum when~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}.$

questions.solution:
\left(\sin^{- 1}x\right)2 - \left(\cos^{- 1}x\right)2 = a$

Let~$\sin^{- 1}\left(x\right) = t$

$x = sint$

\left(\sin^{- 1}sint\right)2 - \left(\cos^{- 1}sint\right)2 = a$

$t^{2} - \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - t\right)2 = a$

$t^{2} - \left(\dfrac{\pi2}{4} + t^{2} - \pit\right) = a$

$t = \dfrac{a}{π} + \dfrac{π}{4}$

$= sin\dfrac{2a}{π}$

questions.q: Considering only the principal values of inverse trigonometric functions, the number of positive real values of $x$ satisfying $\tan^{- 1} ( x ) + \tan^{- 1} ( 2x ) = \dfrac{π}{4}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,

$f\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}x + \tan^{- 1}2x$

Now, differentiating the above function we get,

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}} + \dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^{2}}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) > 0; ∀ x \in R$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}f \left(x\right) = \pi\text{and}\lim_{x \to - \i$i$infty}f\left(x\right) = - \pi$

Hence, $f\left(x\right)$ is monotonically increasing for $x \in R$ and the range of $f \left(x\right)$ is \left(- \pi, \pi\right).$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{π}{4}$has exactly one solution for $x > 0$.

$

questions.q: For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \ne 0$. If $\sin^{- 1}\alpha + \sin^{- 1}\beta + \sin^{- 1}\gamma = \pi$ and \left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)\left(\alpha - \gamma + \beta\right) = 3\alpha\beta$, then $\gamma$ equal to$

questions.solution:
Given: $\sin^{- 1}\alpha + \sin^{- 1}\beta + \sin^{- 1}\gamma = \pi$

Let, $\sin^{- 1}\alpha = A, \sin^{- 1}\beta = B, \sin^{- 1}\gamma = C$

$⇒ A + B + C = \pi$

Also, $\alpha = sinA, \beta = sinB, \gamma = sinC . . . \left(i\right)$

It is given that, \left(\alpha + \beta\right)$2 - {γ}^{2} = $3\alpha\beta.

$⇒ {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} - {γ}^{2} = $\alpha\beta

$⇒ \sin^{2}A + \sin^{2}B - \sin^{2}C = sinAsinB$

$⇒ \sin^{2}A + $sin\left($B + C\$right)sin\left($B - C\right) = sinAsinB$

$⇒ \sin^{2}A + $sin\left(\pi -$A\$right)sin\left($B - C\right) = sinAsinB$

$⇒ \sin^{2}A + $sinAsin\left($B - C\right) = sinAsinB$

$⇒ $sinA\left[$sinA + $sin\left($B - C\right)\right] = sinAsinB$

$⇒ $sinA\left[$sinA + $sin\left($B - C\right)\right] - sinAsinB = 0$

$⇒ $sinA\left[$sinA + $sin\left($B - C\right) - sinB\right] = 0$

$⇒ $sinA\l$left[sin\left($B + C\right) + $sin\left($B - C\right) - sinB\right] = 0$

$⇒ $sinA\left[$2sinBcosC - sinB\right] = 0$

$⇒ $sinAsinB\left[$2cosC - 1\right] = 0$

$⇒ sinA = $0\text{or}$sinB = $0\text{or}$cosC = $\dfrac{1}{2}

It is given that, \alpha, \beta, \gamma \ne$0$

$⇒ cosC = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ sinC = $\dfrac{3}{2}

$⇒ $\gamma = \dfrac{3}{2}

$

questions.q:
If the sum of all the solutions of
$\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\right) + \cot^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \dfrac{π}{3}$,~$- 1 < x < 1, x \ne 0$, is $\alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\right) + \cot^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \dfrac{π}{3}$~where~$x \in \left(-1, 1\right)$

Case~$1$: When~$x < 0$, then

$\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\right) + \cot^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1}x + \pi + 2\tan^{- 1}x = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ 4\tan^{- 1}x = - \pi + \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ 4\tan^{- 1}x = - \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}x = - \dfrac{π}{6}$

$⇒ x = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

Case~$2$:~When~$x \ge 0$,

$\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\right) + \cot^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ 2\tan^{- 1}x + 2\tan^{- 1}x = \dfrac{π}{3}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}x = \dfrac{π}{12}$

$⇒ x = 2 - \sqrt{3}$

So, sum of solution will be~

$\dfrac{- 1}{3} + 2 - \sqrt{3} = 2 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now, on comparing with~$\alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$,~we get

$\alpha = 2&

$
